Verkal Ozovar (Y63)

Region (English scoring table): Haless.

One-line profile: Build an almost immobile Nephrite Dwarf hold, weave the surrounding countries into a network of protected states, and reshape Haless through runes and subjects.

Story: High｜Mission-tree length: Long (50 direct missions)｜Mission-tree update: locally supports EU4 v1.37.5.0; old development roadmaps do not replace the current files｜Uniqueness: Very high｜Tedium: Medium-high (subject loyalty and interface management)｜Early pressure: Medium｜Expansion: Extremely high through subjects, low through direct domestic expansion

An old empire in the mountains

In 1444, Verkal Ozovar is a Nephrite Dwarf kingdom following the Dwarven Pantheon, with its capital fixed in a hold and several friendly Halessi countries around it. It looks like a tiny mountain polity; the offline Wiki shows another side. Around 3500 BA, Grônstunad built an outpost in the Phokhao Range, and after the hold fell, surviving dwarves struggled to migrate there. Millennia of accumulation made this hold an ancient centre preserving old knowledge and traditions of self-rule, not a temporary colonial station. [Local history script][Wiki source]

At its height, Verkal Ozovar did not rule by annexing every piece of land itself. It offered institutions, knowledge and security to Kai tribes in exchange for vassalization. This relationship, beginning around 1650 BA, once covered a broad area; Bokai, Sikai and other groups later rebelled or became independent, and the old network contracted sharply. The Wiki leaves both sides visible: protection and modernization, but also humans seeking autonomy. The entire protectorate relationship should not be written as an equal alliance, and every revolt should not be treated as betrayal. The small 1444 territory is the result of a long retreat. [Wiki source]

Expansion without swallowing land

The current game files make the “protector” a special subject institution. The player can keep the mountain hold compact while assigning surface expansion, warfare and administration to protected countries; the price is maintaining the loyalty and effectiveness of those relationships. This differs sharply from the usual Dwarven “mine–colonize–rule directly” loop: the real realm is the subject network, not Verkal Ozovar's own province colour. Subjects are not permanently stable because of a single oath; control pressure grows with the network. [Local script]

The rune interface is the second national core. Small runes can be changed periodically, while large runes are combined by category with a limited number equipped at once. The player must adapt them to construction, war or diplomacy rather than leaving one permanent set of numbers active. The Jade-seeking events pursue scattered Nephrite Dwarves and ancient techniques, linking the hold's historical memory to its mechanics. The Dwarven Pantheon and runic knowledge also enter statecraft progressively; they are not all unlocked at the start. [Local script][Local event text]

The second half of the mission tree pushes this protection system across Haless: who needs protection, who accepts runes and institutional influence, and how Verkal Ozovar should lead, rather than simply copying an ancient empire. It can manage one province from the mountain, but it cannot focus only on that province; planning wars and economies for allies and subjects is the tree's real workload. The current scripts do not confirm a mandatory Tag change into a formable country. The campaign's protagonist remains Y63. [Local script]

The opening strategy is therefore not to paint every province around the capital as your own, but to make the hold capable of supporting a suzerain's position: construction, finances and rune configuration determine whether the promise of protection can be kept. In the middle game, watch the role each protectorate plays in war and avoid taking on more subjects than you can coordinate. In the late game, the old question returns: when the dwarves on the mountain command the surrounding countries again, do the surface human states gain security and development, or merely enter another unequal order? The missions provide organization and expansion directions; they do not answer that political question for the player. [Local script][Wiki source]

Mountain-hold tradition, the Dwarven Pantheon and runic technology should not be collapsed into a generic “Dwarf bonus.” The old history explains why Verkal Ozovar can claim to be a centre of knowledge; religion and events explain how it searches for its scattered kin; the rune interface requires the player to reconfigure limited capabilities in response to circumstances. Together, these make the tree visibly different from ordinary hold gameplay. [Wiki source][Local script]

An old official roadmap listed Verkal Ozovar as future content about “Dwarves, descendants and magic”; a later religion development diary added its Grônstunad-colony background and Dwarven Pantheon route. These explain design direction, but cannot replace current files as proof of particular rune effects. Two player posts praised “single-province management and a Haless-wide subject network” and also mentioned late-game subject management and performance burdens; these remain observations from older versions. [Official development diaries][Community views]

If story is your priority, Verkal Ozovar is not simply about taking revenge on former rebels. It must prove that it still possesses knowledge, wealth and the capacity to protect before surrounding countries accept its arrangements. The Kai rebellions in the old history cast a real shadow over this project: rebuilding relationships can be mutually beneficial, or it can reproduce domination. The subject system turns that historical question into a daily operation. [Wiki source][Local script]

Personality and recommendation

The v2.1 personality coordinates are Expansion 58/100｜Authoritarianism 78/100｜Magic↔Artifice 78/100 (100 = magic, 0 = artifice; thematic intensity 73/100)｜Pluralism 67/100.

The v2.1 values assessment is Neutral (66/100), with a stable trajectory. Knowledge-sharing, protection and trade have positive evidence; old history and current mechanics both retain hierarchical control over subjects, so protection cannot be called equal autonomy, while there is not enough evidence to equate it with slavery. The old protection, knowledge-sharing and mutually beneficial trade support the positive assessment; subject hierarchy and past human rebellions show that “protection” does not mean the other side retains complete autonomy forever. There is insufficient evidence to equate the protectorate system with slavery, and being a subject empire is not by itself evidence of evil. It suits players who enjoy compact development, rune combinations, indirect rule and long-term alliance management; players who only want to annex land personally and dislike subject loyalty and extensive diplomacy will find it tedious. [Local script][Wiki source]

Fixed Wiki revisions, script locations and version boundaries are listed on the evidence page.

National Ideas

The following reproduces the current local national-idea text and script effects. Traditions apply when the set is adopted; the seven ideas unlock in sequence as points are invested, and the ambition applies after all seven are unlocked. Only national ideas are listed: racial, government and mission bonuses are excluded. A successor idea set does not automatically stack with the earlier set. Idea descriptions may recall history or express future aspirations; they do not automatically establish events already completed in 1444. Names and complete descriptions use the current Mod’s English localisation. Alternative and predecessor/successor sets remain separately conditional, including whether new ideas are accepted on formation.

Effect units inherited from the source data are reproduced for parity, not revalidated here; suspicious percentages or script-valued effects require separate review. Raw script values are shown where appropriate.

Verkal Ozovar (Y63) — Nephrite Ideas

Set ID: Y63_ideas. Source: project-verified Mod script (public artifact omits local path and line offsets).

Applicability condition (source script):

    trigger = {
        tag = Y63
    }

Nephrite Traditions

  • Can fabricate claims for vassals: Allowed (can_fabricate_for_vassals; raw value yes).

  • Liberty Desire in Subjects on the Same Continent: +2500% (reduced_liberty_desire_on_same_continent; raw value 25).

1. The Mountain King

Verkal Ozovar has loomed high over the lands of the Hinphat since they were but mere tribes roaming the plains, shadowed by the Phokhao Range. For eons we have been their guiding hand as their Mountain Kings, uplifting them into civility in return for regular tribute and servitude.

  • Vassal force limit contribution: +100% (vassal_forcelimit_bonus; raw value 1).

2. Lessons of the Jadefall

When the holds of the Jade Mines fell, their inhabitants were forced to flee, trekking through the exotic and diverse realms of Haless before finally reaching our mighty Nephrite Hold. The refugees picked up on as much knowledge as they could during their travels, developing new insights into their previously conservative dwarven mindset. With such extensive knowledge of cultural customs from across Haless, our emissaries have an easy time ingratiating themselves with foreign powers.

  • Diplomatic reputation: +100% (diplomatic_reputation; raw value 1).

3. Riches of Phokhao

Most that look upon the Phokhao range see only the rough, jagged stone of the mountains, not knowing of the great wealth of gems and ores hidden deep within, only accessible to those with the ingenuity and determination of a dwarf.

  • Production efficiency: +10% (production_efficiency; raw value 0.1).

4. Bring the Lost Home

Many of our displaced kin, heirs of the Jadefall, reside in small surface towns and squalorous slums across Haless, unable to truly find new homes among the humans and harimari. This is a call for them to flock to the verdant gates of Verkal Ozovar, to finally reside among brothers once again.

  • Development cost: -15% (development_cost; raw value -0.15).

5. Scions of Grônstunad

Grônstunad was the greatest hold of the eastern Serpentspine, its power even rivalling that of Amldihr and outlasting the old capital of Aul-Dwarov. Even she was not to last however, as those goblinoid bastards overran her gates and desecrated her hallowed halls of jade. We are the descendents and heirs to those that escaped the fall of Grônstunad, and we are determined to live up to our illustrious legacy.

  • Prestige: +1 (prestige; raw value 1).

6. Wizards of Ozovar

Magic comes easier to the inhabitants of Verkal Ozovar than most other dwarves in the form of runesmithing, though the arcane arts may still be a relative rarity amongst our people compared to the likes of humans or elves.

Enough runesmiths practice their craft within our halls to risk themselves on the frontlines of battle, concocting grand runic batteries to fell our foes in addition to traditional spellcraft.

  • Shock damage: +10% (shock_damage; raw value 0.1).

7. Viridescent Legion

The Viridescent Legion is the elite guard of Verkal Ozovar, each member personally chosen by the king of our hold to serve for life and clad in opulent enchanted Nephrite armor. These fine warriors lead the armies of Ozovar as their gleaming vanguard, standing as the pride of the Citadel of the East.

  • fire_damage_received: -10% (fire_damage_received; raw value -0.1).

Nephrite Ambition

  • Improve relations: +25% (improve_relation_modifier; raw value 0.25).
